dish: Tavern-style thin crust, party-cut, cash only
w: Bridgeport's tavern-style institution since 1960 — greasy, generously topped thin pies cut in squares, counter service, cash only.

dish: Italian beef with thick-cut slices and a chickpea-studded hot mix
w: South Siders' pick for the city's best beef — one of the biggest sandwiches in town, thicker slices that stay tender (Infatuation 8.0).

dish: Quarter-pound burger with grilled onions, beef-tallow fries, thick chocolate shake
w: Beverly's wood-panelled burger shop since 1942 — fresh-ground round on a feather-light bun, fries cooked in beef tallow.

dish: Griddled fresh-ground burgers, hand-cut fries, milkshakes
w: Evanston's old-school burger counter (2009) — the North Shore's burger benchmark on Infatuation's and Time Out's Evanston lists.

dish: Carnitas by the pound, chicharrón, weekend birria de chivo
w: Pilsen carnitas house opened by Pedro Duarte in 1981 — pork cooked in its own fat, sold by weight; weekend lines out the door.

dish: Square-cut pizza, house-roasted Italian beef and meats, gelato (14% milk, no eggs)
w: Cicero corner grocery turned Italian deli-pizzeria, run by Neapolitan immigrant Joe Quercia since 1973 — hot-table Italian, pizza and some of the area's best gelato.

dish: Flaming saganaki, taramosalata, wood-fired octopus and souvlaki
w: Live-fire Greek from James Beard winner Jimmy Bannos Jr. — named to the New York Times' best-restaurants-in-America list.

dish: Chinese-American bar plates (crab rangoon, Peking-style dishes) with cocktails
w: Bucktown Chinese-American cocktail bar with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

dish: Cafeteria-line breakfast — steak and eggs, the 'Obama' Mediterranean omelet
w: Hyde Park cafeteria since 1921, one of the oldest in the US — Barack Obama's regular, his orders still on the board. Cash only.

address: 3511 S Martin Luther King Dr, Chicago, IL 60653
dish: Chicken yassa (onion-lemon-mustard), saka saka, fataya
w: Senegalese family restaurant (2004, Bronzeville since 2015) — called one of the city's best African restaurants; South Side Weekly's 'Best Resurrection' after a fire.

dish: Hickory-smoked rib tips and ribs in an aquarium smoker, honey-tinged sauce
w: Chicago-style aquarium-smoker barbecue, in Bronzeville since 2015 — a Choose Chicago South Side pick. Cash only.

dish: Soul-food breakfast buffet, fried chicken, biscuits, peach cobbler
w: Bronzeville soul-food dining room since 1993 — Roadfood rates it 'Excellent / Worth a Detour'.

dish: The 'Mutt' — rib tips, hot link and wings on fries, house sauce
w: Evanston barbecue institution of the late Hecky Powell — the North Shore's rib-tip and sauce benchmark (Axios rib-tip Food Fight).

dish: The baked apple pancake — caramelized cinnamon-sugar apples
w: The 1960 Wilmette original of the North Shore pancake family (in Ordinary People) — Zagat's 'best breakfast, bar none'.

dish: Barbecue beef and pork sandwiches, ribs, 14-hour brisket
w: Opened 1930 — the oldest continuously operating barbecue restaurant in the Chicago area, on Thatcher Avenue since the 1940s.

dish: Swedish pancakes with lingonberries, falukorv, meatballs with gravy
w: Andersonville's tiny Swedish breakfast room with Viking art — the last of the neighbourhood's old Swedish diners.

dish: Deep dish on the buttercrust with the Malnati Chicago Classic sausage patty
w: The 1971 original of Lou Malnati's — where the family's buttercrust deep dish began, before it became Chicago's best-known deep-dish name.

dish: Roots-music shows with a tavern bar; American Music Festival every July 4th weekend
w: Berwyn roots-music club and tavern (FitzGerald family since 1980, a music hall since the 1930s) — in 2025 the first Illinois music venue on the National Register.

dish: House-brewed ales (Sgt. Reckless pale) with Southern-style smoked plates
w: Beverly's award-winning brewpub (2013) — a 6,000 sq ft Western Avenue taproom with house beer and Southern-leaning food.

address: 8249 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60619
dish: Eight-inch 'Texas' donuts and buttermilk cake donuts, 24 hours
w: Chatham's round-the-clock donut shop — its glazed made the Daily Meal's America's 25 best; often called the best donuts on the South Side.
